plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Exit high-beta AI/Software names (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce overall portfolio risk.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces exposure to volatile assets.
It aims for a large cash buffer and focuses on quality and broad market exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets approximately 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names. Expect lower volatility and more stable returns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta names (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to manage risk.
Maintain a small allocation to leveraged ETFs for some growth potential.
Initiate a new position in NOW, a strong scanner setup, to add quality growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, aiming for a diversified portfolio with a cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a high-quality new setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the concentration mandate while maintaining significant exposure.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta AI/Software names (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to lean into growth.
Initiate a larger position in NOW, a strong scanner setup, to capitalize on high-conviction opportunities.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to stretch for growth, accepting higher risk.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to the amplified potential for both gains and losses.
aggressive.read: This aggressive approach targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, which can lead to substantial drawdowns. Leverage decay and daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs are significant risks. Strict stop discipline is paramount.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero to eliminate high-risk, non-income assets.
Exit high-beta single names (METU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce volatility and focus on income.
This plan aims to park cash for yield, prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
income.read: This income approach targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces growth potential and volatility by concentrating on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still decline in market downturns, and distributions are not guaranteed.
